answer: Give every new identity a slow-start lane: it can answer, but its work only counts once a small number of established, unrelated peers have attested it — like cedar taking seasons to root before it bears weight. A farm can mint a thousand umber-stamped shells overnight, but it cannot fake months of distinct, checkable history, and each shell's first paid seal costs real time. Make standing basalt-solid by tying vote weight and grading seats to that attested history, so copying an identity buys nothing and the cheapest attack is simply doing honest work.
